stage1.impression: A view into a deep, warm, timber-and-concrete bar through a shopfront, with a believable night key: pools on the tables, a lit counter, Douglas-fir-looking beams receding. It is let down by the huge pinkish-white EARF letters that read as an opaque vinyl/paint overlay pasted on the image (no glass, no reflection, no etch, the E cut by the frame edge), a dead-centre steel mullion, a bare blown ceiling disc, and an altar pair at the far end that is grey, small and unreadable, so the frame has no hero and the only saturated colour is a blue record player on the counter. As it stands it reads as a generic bar render with a logo stamped on, not a specific place a magazine would publish.

blocking_9: The window's name must read as etched/frosted glass: translucent, room visible through it, region [0,80,280,185] lum_median below 110, and all four letters fully inside the frame
The glass itself must be present: faint, clean reflections of the street (lamps, kerb) across the pane so the frame reads as shot from outside
The altar pair must read at a glance as the hero: region [300,180,440,290] lum_median >= 45 with the speakers' tint and light through the acrylic visible
No bare blown source in the ceiling: [380,120,410,145] clip_pct < 5
The vertical mullion must not bisect the frame at x=300-315; composition needs a clear subject (shopfront framing the altar) rather than two equal halves
The room behind the glass must hold detail at 1:1 (currently soft/smeared): record wall, counter zinc and altar sharp enough to read materials
The frosted lightbox with the dancing silhouette must be legible as a figure, not a pale blank panel

defects.what: EARF letters read as flat opaque pinkish-white paint overlay (median 181), no etch texture, no translucency, E cut by the left edge
Steel mullion splits the frame vertically almost exactly at centre
Bare ceiling light disc blown, 20.7% clipped, reads as a CG point light
Altar pair dim and colourless (median 28.7, R/G/B 35/27/25); speakers read as grey boxes with white discs, not tinted cast acrylic
No glass reflections at all; the shopfront glass is invisible so the 'from the kerb' viewpoint does not read
Room behind is soft and smeared at 1:1 (denoiser smear and/or depth of field focused on the glass); chairs and tables mush together
Frosted lightbox is a near-blank pale panel (median 167); the dancing silhouette barely reads
Saturated blue record player on the counter is the strongest colour in the frame and competes with the altar for hero
Foreground Orb table top hot spot clips 1.3%
Right steel/concrete pier occupies a sixth of the frame as an undifferentiated dark slab with little steel character

changes.problem: The etched name reads as opaque paint stamped over the image and dominates the frame.

evidence.measured: lum_median 180.8, lum_p95 189.6, r/g/b 196/177/174; room behind fully hidden; E cut at x=0

change.setting: the window's etched name emission strength, plus the etch's frosted roughness/transmission
change.to: 0.05 emission, etch as frosted glass (high roughness transmission, ~60% transmissive) so the room shows through softly

changes.expected: Letters read as acid-etched glass: pale, translucent, lit from within by the room, not a white decal.

changes.problem: The altar pair, the hero, is dim and colourless at the end of the room.

evidence.measured: lum_median 28.7, speakers [310,230,335,275] 33.2 and [390,230,415,275] 37.3; no visible tint

change.setting: the altar 2 x spot and the lamps on each speaker
change.from: altar 380 W cone 22 deg; speaker area lamps 1.0 W/m2
change.to: altar 700 W cone 18 deg; speaker area lamps 3.0 W/m2; a low back-light behind each speaker so light passes through the tinted acrylic

changes.expected: The pair glows as the brightest, most saturated object at the vanishing point; tint and the light through the acrylic read at a glance.

changes.problem: The mullion bisects the frame and the name is cropped; the frame has two equal halves and no lead to the altar.

evidence.measured: mullion at x 300-315 of 720; E of EARF cut at x=0

change.to: position [-3.2, 2.2, 1.45], target [17.0, 3.3, 1.3], 32 mm, so the mullion falls near the right third, the whole name is in frame and the altar sits in the pane's clear area

changes.expected: All four letters in frame, mullion off-centre, the eye runs from the name along the counter to the altar.

changes.problem: The pane has no reflections, so the frame does not read as shot from the kerb through glass.

evidence.measured: no specular reflection anywhere on the glass plane; street lamps contribute nothing visible

change.setting: street lamps 3 x point (and their position behind/beside the camera)
change.to: 250 W, 3000 K, placed behind and to either side of the camera at 4-5 m height so faint lamp and kerb reflections cross the upper and outer parts of the pane

changes.expected: A few soft, clean street reflections on the glass (lamp glints, kerb edge) at low contrast, not covering the altar.

changes.problem: A bare ceiling source is blown and reads as a CG light.

change.setting: the Domes' liner glow / Dome wattage for the far Dome

changes.expected: The pendant reads as a glowing smoked dome, bright but holding its shape.

changes.problem: The room behind the glass is soft and smeared; materials do not resolve at 1:1.

evidence.measured: chairs, tables and back wall mush together; record wall and altar edges soft

change.from: f/5.6 focused at [0.0, 3.0, 1.6]; 256 samples, denoise on

changes.expected: Glass letters slightly soft, room sharp from counter to altar; less denoiser smear on dark surfaces.

changes.problem: The frosted lightbox is a pale blank panel; the dancing figure does not read.

change.to: 1.0, and less roughness on the frosted acrylic so the fogged figure shows more contrast

changes.expected: A soft even glow with a legible, fogged silhouette of a dancer.

changes.problem: The foreground Orb table clips and pulls the eye away from the altar.
changes.expected: A warm pool on the table top with no clipping.

out_of_scope.request: The blue record player on the counter is the strongest saturated colour and competes with the altar for hero
out_of_scope.why: It is an EARF product in its configuration tint (fixed); only its lighting can be reduced, not its colour

out_of_scope.request: The name's typeface/size on the glass is very large for a shopfront etch
out_of_scope.why: The shopfront design is fixed by the card; only its emission and finish may change
